title: Your first five minutes
subtitle: A clear first conversation with Genesis AI

scenes.title:
Your first
five minutes
scenes.body:
Connect a model. Start a conversation.
Shape an answer you can use.

scenes.title: One useful conversation
items: Connect the model that answers you
Choose local or cloud setup
Leave optional extras for later
Send a small, clear request
Ask for a better-fitting answer
scenes.note: Genesis should already be installed on Windows. First downloads or cloud setup need internet.

scenes.title: The app and the model
scenes.body: Genesis is the app you use. The model is the part that works out an answer. Connect one working model before your first conversation.
scenes.note: You can choose automatic setup or open More options.

scenes.title: Start with automatic setup
scenes.body: Choose “Set up Genesis AI for me” to let Genesis prepare the local setup. It offers a model sized for your computer and downloads what it needs.
scenes.note: Leave Genesis open until the download finishes.

scenes.title: Already have a model?
scenes.body: Open “More options” if you want to choose a cloud service or a local model yourself. Automatic setup is the easiest starting route when you are new.
scenes.note: Checkpoint: you can find both setup routes.

scenes.title: Local or cloud?

cards.title: LOCAL
cards.body:
The model runs on your computer.

Download it first. Once ready, the model can answer offline. Internet-dependent tools still need a connection.

cards.title: CLOUD
cards.body:
A service answers over the internet.

Connect that service with its API key and exact model name. The provider may charge for usage.

scenes.note: Choose the route that fits your computer and the service you already use.

scenes.title: Pick your connection
scenes.body: In More options, choose Cloud, Ollama or llama.cpp. Cloud connects a provider. Ollama and llama.cpp are local routes for a model you manage yourself.
scenes.note: If you are starting fresh locally, you can return to automatic setup.

scenes.title: A key is a private credential
scenes.body: For cloud setup, select your provider and enter its API key. A key lets Genesis use that service. Keep it private; do not put it in a conversation or share it.
scenes.note: The example screen uses a placeholder, not a real key.

scenes.title: Use the exact model name
scenes.body: Enter the model name supported by your chosen provider. A saved model name alone does not download a local model. Local setup also needs a model installed and available.
scenes.note: Use the name supplied by the service or your local model server.

scenes.title: Test before you continue
scenes.body: Use the connection test, then finish setup when it reports success. If the test fails, recheck the provider, key and model name before trying your first message.
scenes.note: Checkpoint: setup reports success. This screenshot is an example, not a successful live test.

scenes.title: You can begin with the basics
scenes.body: Once setup finishes, you reach the conversation. Better speech recognition, browser setup and a phone connection are optional extras. You can return to them later.
scenes.note: Open Settings → Finish setting up when you are ready.

scenes.title: Add extras when you need them
items: Speech recognition: for talking to Genesis
Browser setup: for connected browser work
Phone connection: for using your phone
scenes.note: You can skip an extra now and return through Settings or Help. Checkpoint: you know where to resume setup.

scenes.title: Open Conversation
scenes.body: Click Conversation in the left panel. Start with an ordinary question or a small request. You do not need special commands to explain what you want.
scenes.note: For this first exercise, ask Genesis to help plan three easy dinners.

scenes.title: Find the message box
scenes.body: Click the message box at the bottom of the conversation. Write a request that says what you want, and add a useful constraint or an instruction about how to begin.
scenes.note: Write naturally. The first exercise uses an ordinary dinner-planning request.

scenes.title: Give it a useful starting point
scenes.quote:
Help me plan three easy dinners.
Ask me what food I have first.
scenes.body: The first sentence names the outcome. The second tells Genesis to ask a question before it makes the plan.
scenes.note: Type this in your own conversation. Pause the video here if you want to try it.

scenes.title: Send when you are ready
scenes.body: Press Enter to send, or click the round arrow button. Use Shift+Enter if you want a new line without sending your message yet.
scenes.note: Read your draft before sending. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line.

scenes.title: Answer the next question
scenes.question: What ingredients do you already have?
scenes.answer:
I have rice, eggs, carrots and beans.
Each dinner should take under 20 minutes.
scenes.body: Your reply supplies facts and a time limit. Genesis can use those details to make the plan more relevant.
scenes.note: This is an illustrative exchange. Your model’s exact wording and answer may differ.

scenes.title: Did your first message work?
items: Your request appears in Conversation
Genesis responds to your request
You can answer its next question
scenes.note: If no answer arrives, return to Settings → Models and check your connection. Do not assume a saved name means the model is ready.

scenes.title: Ask for a change
scenes.quote:
Make that simpler.
Keep each dinner under 20 minutes.
scenes.body: You can follow up in the same conversation. Be specific about what should change: complexity, time, ingredients, length or tone.
scenes.note: You do not need to start over just because the first answer needs a revision.

scenes.title: Choose the format you need
scenes.quote:
Put it in a shopping list.
Leave out the food I already have.
scenes.body: Ask for a useful format: a list, a table, a shorter explanation or a first draft. For our dinner example, a shopping list turns the plan into a next action.
scenes.note: Read the list and correct anything that does not fit your needs.

scenes.title: Check. Correct. Continue.
items: Read the answer before relying on it
Tell Genesis when a detail is wrong
Ask it to revise the part that needs work
scenes.note: Genesis can help with writing, explanations, files, research and tasks. Connected tools make more actions available; setup and permissions still matter.

scenes.title: Make one answer fit your life
items: Ask for three easy dinners
Reply with your ingredients and time limit
Ask for a simpler version
Turn it into a shopping list
scenes.note: Checkpoint: you have a useful answer and know how to ask for a change. Pause and try this sequence in your own conversation.

scenes.title: From setup to a useful answer
items: One connected model, local or cloud
Optional extras can wait
A clear request and a useful follow-up
Your own review of the final answer
scenes.note: Next in the course: find your way around the Genesis interface. Keep this lesson nearby if you need to repeat a step.

scenes.title:
Start small.
Make it useful.
scenes.body:
One clear request. One thoughtful follow-up.
An answer you have checked.
